findings.title: fetch_error_details mis-associates error ids with event data
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id, and entries for missing events may be `None`. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` relies on the dict preserving the exact order of `node_ids` and on every id being present; the `if data is not None` filter is applied *after* zipping, so as soon as one event is missing (or the backend returns keys in a different order) every subsequent report gets the wrong `id` attached to the wrong title/message/timestamp. Iterate over `node_ids` paired with `error_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check is defeated by falsy values and both-absent case
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report with `age: 0` (a legitimate value meaning "just now") plus a `timestamp` passes validation, because `0` is falsy. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` instead. Additionally, since both fields are `required=False` and the checks only fire inside the respective field validators, a report containing *neither* `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted, although the spec requires one of them; a `validate()` level check is needed. `age` also lacks a `min_value`, unlike `timestamp`.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a per-issue event fetch inside comment generation
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for every issue included in a PR comment. `get_recommended_event` performs a Snuba/eventstore query, so building a comment for 5 issues now triggers 5 extra event lookups plus environment lookups per PR comment task, on a path that previously only read fields already loaded on the Group. Consider batching or using cached group metadata (e.g. `GroupEnvironment`) instead.

findings.title: New table widget path renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. Any organization with the flag on will see every dashboard table widget render completely empty. Either wire the real data through or keep this behind code that is not reachable.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature gate and may use anonymous user id
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` check, so the event is emitted even for orgs without the feature (which get a 404), inflating the metric. Also, for org-auth-token authenticated requests `request.user` is an anonymous user, so `request.user.id` will be `None`; consider guarding with `getattr(request.user, "id", None)` and moving the record after the feature check.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions may be missing keys used by get_condition_query_groups
findings.body: `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` is now computed once from `event_data.dcg_ids`, but `get_condition_query_groups` previously computed it from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()` and indexes `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` directly. If the two id sets ever diverge, this raises a `KeyError` and fails the whole delayed-workflow batch rather than skipping one group. Use `.get(dcg.id, [])` or assert the sets are equal.
